text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Two women are in a critical condition after a disgruntled employee went on a shooting rampage at the offices of the Windhoek Society for the Prevention of Cruelty against Animals (SPCA). One of the wounded is Ida Africa, wife of DTA politician Ben Africa.

- Prime Minister Hage Geingob has challenged European Union ambassadors to pinpoint cases where homosexuals had been victimised in Namibia, after widespread criticism of last week's anti-gay statement by the ruling SWAPO party.

- Southern African Development Community secretary general, Kaire Mbuende, announced a concerted drive to tackle productivity within SADC states, when he briefed the media on the theme of the 1997 consultative conference.
- Doubts over the SADC region's international competitiveness were voiced at the trade group's annual consultative conference.
